fatal_errors: The essential comparison between as-printed and 750°C/50 h precipitation-aged states is absent.
The proposed outer Al2O3/inner Cr2O3 architecture reverses the target behavior, which centers on a continuous protective Cr-rich layer and an inner discontinuous Al/Ti-rich region.
The baseline is not compositionally or microstructurally controlled, so differences cannot be attributed specifically to selective Al/Cr oxidation.
The predicted benefit of an optimized alloy does not reproduce the observed result that the aged state gains more mass than the as-printed state.
Cited evidence E3 explicitly reports external chromia followed by internal alumina, contradicting the proposed layer ordering.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses high-temperature oxidation of Al-Co-Cr-Fe-Ni MPEAs and proposes measurable diffusion-barrier behavior, so it is scientifically plausible in broad terms. It does not reconstruct the paper's governing test: aging-induced L12/L21 precipitation, local Cr depletion, and added interfaces versus a uniform-Cr as-printed baseline. Consequently it misses the observed delayed chromia protection and higher oxidation of the aged material. Its 800–1200°C, 25 h static/cyclic exposure only partially overlaps the 600–1200°C, up-to-96 h isothermal study and omits the approximately 900°C kinetic transition. TGA and scale characterization could test the alternative hypothesis, but the vague baseline and simultaneous composition differences would confound attribution. The evidence supports the general importance of Al2O3, Cr2O3, chemistry, and microstructure, but does not validate the asserted scale ordering and partly contradicts it.
